title: Token surface consistency sweep + mobile Safari/Firefox touch regressions
creator: Maya Lopez
description: Overview: A cross-platform sweep uncovered a set of inconsistent design token usages and several interaction regressions on mobile Safari and Firefox for components in the UI kit (buttons, tables, and charts). This ticket consolidates the investigation, documents repros, triages severity, and defines fixes and acceptance criteria. Scope includes token naming/usage (spacing, radii, elevation), button active/press states on iOS, sticky table header behavior on Safari mobile, and SVG/chart rendering quirks in Firefox (stroke alignment, pixel snapping).
symptoms_observed: Pressed state opacity not applied on iOS for primary button
Sticky table header jumps on scroll in Safari mobile
Line chart hairlines render thinner in Firefox causing aliasing
Token scale mismatch: spacing token small-03 used where small-02 expected
Tooltip hit area clipped on small screens
acceptance_criteria: All token mismatches identified and replaced with canonical tokens in the UI kit library
Button active/pressed visual parity across Chrome, Firefox, iOS Safari and Android Chrome (manual QA + automated visual snapshots)
Sticky table header stable on iOS Safari and Android Chrome with no layout jump on scroll
Charts render with consistent stroke weight/anti-aliasing in Firefox (visual diff < 2% threshold) and Chrome
New visual regression tests added to Chromatic/Percy for impacted components
QA checklist and regression test plan committed to repo and linked in ticket
reproduction_steps: Open components page in Figma/Storybook on iPhone-size viewport in Safari and Firefox for Android emulator
For buttons: tap/press primary and secondary buttons and observe active/pressed styles and hit area
For tables: scroll long table with sticky header and observe header jump or overlap
For charts: load line/bar charts in Firefox desktop and compare stroke rendering to Chrome; capture screenshot at 100% zoom
Record sequence in Loom and attach to ticket for developer reference
triage_notes: Initial severity: medium — visual regressions affecting exploratory flows, not blocking core functionality
Customer impact: medium for embedded dashboards and mobile admin flows; low for public browsing
Suggested owners: design token audit (Design), Button behavior fix (Frontend Eng), Table sticky header fix (Frontend Eng), Chart SVG fix (Rendering/Platform Eng)
Temporary mitigation: add fallback tokens and increase touch hit area via utility class in next patch release
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Decide to normalize spacing tokens under token aliasing layer rather than refactor every component immediately — will add linter rule to flag deprecated token usage
2026-03-12: For mobile button pressed state, use -webkit-tap-highlight-color: rgba(0,0,0,0) + explicit active class applied via touchstart/touchend in React wrapper
2026-03-12: Chart rendering in Firefox: increase stroke-width by 0.25px and use shape-rendering: geometricPrecision for SVG paths where anti-aliasing differs
2026-03-13: Sticky header: switch from position: sticky to JS-assisted translateY shim on iOS Safari as a short-term fix; file follow-up to remove when Safari fixes enough
implementation_notes: Add eslint-plugin-design-tokens rule to flag deprecated tokens during build
Introduce tokens/aliases.json to map old tokens to canonical names and a codemod to migrate component usage
Create Storybook stories at iPhone SE and Pixel 4 sizes for manual QA gating
Add end-to-end Cypress tests simulating touch events to validate press state and sticky header behavior
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Token alias layer could mask deeper semantic mismatches — Mitigation: run codemod + manual review for high-use components
Risk: JS sticky shim adds runtime complexity — Mitigation: keep shim scoped and documented; set feature-flagged rollout with telemetry
Risk: Visual snapshot noise — Mitigation: capture snapshots with stable fonts, set threshold and use diff ignore regions for animated chart elements
